title: Props, emits and a typed contract between components

videos.script:
A component is only useful if it can be used more than once, with different data each time. {{props}} This lesson is how data gets in, and how news gets out.

Data gets in as props. You will pass a number as text by forgetting one colon, and watch Vue warn and use it anyway.

{{oneway}} Props flow one way. A child that changes one is refused. A child that changes something inside an object prop is not refused, and that is the dangerous case.

{{emits}} News gets out as events. The child says what happened, and the parent decides what it means.

{{contract}} Together, props and events are a component's contract. Everything else about it is private. You will also see what happens to an attribute the contract does not mention.

{{model}} Then defineModel, a prop the child can write to, which is how v-model works on a component of your own.

{{planner}} And then the planner splits into components. A card for each course, and a row for each session that reports a tick and does nothing else.
